*   **Reference Number:** POC-F37F115FED-48372
*   **Requested Service:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression (Laminotomy/Discectomy)
*   **Procedure Code (CPT):** 63030
*   **Ordering Surgeon:** [First Name] Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Appeals Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of the prior authorization request for my lower back disc surgery and decompression (CPT 63030) to be performed by Dr. Reyes. 

The denial letter dated August 23, 2026, states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. However, a review of my clinical history against the plan's governing clinical guidelines demonstrates that I fully satisfy all requirements for this procedure. 

According to my research, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield delegates clinical utilization management for spine surgeries to Carelon Medical Benefits Management. The governing medical policy is the **"Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Spine Surgery"** (Doc ID: MSK03-1125.1-UC0126, Effective Date: November 15, 2025). 

Below, I have mapped my clinical records directly to the clinical indications required under this policy to demonstrate full medical necessity:

### 1. Radicular Pain and Significant Functional Impairment
The policy states that surgical decompression is appropriate for:
> "Initial disc herniation when ALL the following criteria are met:"
> "Radicular pain (radiculitis/radiculopathy) with significant functional impairment or physical exam findings that correlate with radiculopathy or nerve root compression such as:"
> "Reflex changes (asymmetry, decrease, or absence)"
> "Sensory loss (dermatomal)"
> "Weakness (myotomal)"
> "Positive straight leg raise or contralateral straight leg raise"

*   **My Clinical Evidence:** I have suffered from 24 months of progressive lower back pain, which now radiates directly into my right calf (radicular pain/radiculopathy). This has caused severe, documented functional impairment: I am currently unable to stand for more than 10 minutes at a time. Furthermore, my physical examination by Dr. Reyes revealed positive provocative testing on my right side and a neurological deficit corresponding to the L5 nerve root level, matching the required exam findings.

### 2. Confirmatory Advanced Imaging
The policy requires:
> "Documentation of nerve root compression or thecal sac impingement on MRI or other advanced imaging performed within the past 6 months that correlates with clinical findings"

*   **My Clinical Evidence:** A lumbar spine MRI performed on June 30, 2026 (less than two months ago, and well within the required 6-month window) reveals an **L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root**. This objective imaging finding perfectly correlates with my right-sided radicular calf pain, positive provocative exam, and L5 neurological deficit.

### 3. Ruling Out Alternative Pain Sources
The policy requires that:
> "All other reasonable sources of pain have been ruled out"

*   **My Clinical Evidence:** Dr. Reyes has evaluated my condition and ruled out other potential sources of back and leg pain. My pain is structurally and neurologically localized, directly correlating to the L4-L5 disc extrusion and right L5 nerve root compression. I have no active infections, no untreated substance use, and my BMI is 29. I am also a non-smoker, which minimizes surgical risks.

### 4. Failure of Conservative Management
The policy requires:
> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management (Physical therapy optional)"

*   **My Clinical Evidence:** I have extensively exhausted conservative treatment options without lasting relief:
    *   **Physical Therapy:** I completed 10 weeks of supervised, professional physical therapy from April 20, 2026, to June 29, 2026. This included 18 visits focused on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility. This is fully documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
    *   **Medications:** I tried oral NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
    *   **Injections:** I received a lumbar corticosteroid injection on April 13, 2026, which yielded only 2 weeks of partial, temporary relief before my symptoms returned.

### Conclusion

My clinical presentation is the textbook definition of an individual requiring lumbar decompression and discectomy. I have a severe structural disc extrusion compressing a major nerve root, objective neurological deficits, profound functional limitations, and I have failed more than double the required duration of conservative care (10 weeks of physical therapy versus the 6 weeks required by your policy). 

Because my records satisfy every single clinical requirement listed in Carelon’s Spine Surgery guideline, I request that you reverse this denial immediately and authorize CPT code 63030.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this urgent medical matter.

Sincerely,

Rowan Lawson

**Enclosures:**
1. Lumbar Spine MRI Report (dated June 30, 2026)
2. Physical Therapy Discharge Summary (showing 18 visits, April 20, 2026 – June 29, 2026)
3. Clinical Consultation and Exam Notes from Dr. Reyes, MD
4. Documentation of lumbar corticosteroid injection (dated April 13, 2026)
